summary: Selects a format string from a format-state object by index, falling back to the first primary-table string (overriding the stored argument) when the index is out of range, then scans the selected string for a '%s' (115) sequence to choose between varargs and va_list calling conventions and delegates to StringFormatWithBufferOverflowCheck.

operations.description: Load the format-state pointer v2 = *(DWORD**)a1 and read the stored format index v3 from the object.
Range-check v3 against the primary table count and the alternate table start/end bounds; out-of-range indices route to the fallback path.
Alternate-range resolution: v4 = *(char**)(alternate table base + 4 * (v3 - alternate start index)).
Primary-range resolution: v4 = *(char**)(primary table base + 4 * v3).
Fallback when the resolved string pointer is null: write v3 into the stored argument field and use the first primary-table string as the format string.

Scan the selected format string for a null terminator or a '%' (37) character; if the terminator is reached first, return StringFormatWithBufferOverflowCheck(a2, v4, stored arguments) passing the stored argument fields.
After a '%' is found, check whether the following character is not 's' (115); when it is not '%s', call StringFormatWithBufferOverflowCheck with the individual stored arguments (varargs form).
For the '%s' (115) case, return StringFormatWithBufferOverflowCheck(a2, v4, pointer to the stored argument fields) using the va_list-style form.

clean_pseudocode: if (index within primary range) fmt = state->primary_table[index];
else if (index within alternate range) fmt = state->alternate_table[index - state->alternate_start];
if end of string reached before '%': return format(dst, fmt, args...);
if next char != 's': return format(dst, fmt, args...);
